1000610.etyen:
From sør (“south”) + Afrika (“Africa”). The second element is ultimately from Latin Āfrica (“Africa”), the substantivized feminine of āfricus (“African”), from Āfer (“African; member of the Afri”) + -icus (“adjectival suffix”). The Latin name originally referred to the region around Carthage in present-day northeastern Tunisia and was later extended to the entire continent. The ultimate origin of the ethnonym Āfrī (“the Afri”) is uncertain.
Compare the parallel formations Norwegian Nynorsk Sør-Afrika, Danish Sydafrika, Swedish Sydafrika, German Südafrika, Dutch Zuid-Afrika and Afrikaans Suid-A

1004706.etyen:
Named after Stavsjøen, the lake just north of the settlement. The lake name is from stav (“staff, rod”) + sjø (“lake, sea”), probably referring to a straight or staff-like shape.
